amendments.body: Reset `spawn_progress_accum` when the adult population or eligible spawner count drops to zero. The new accumulator is persisted in `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:128-131`, and `spawning()` both consumes it at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:443-444` and returns early at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:425-435` without clearing it. That means a later, unrelated colony can inherit fractional spawn progress from a deleted one. I reproduced this by stepping a 10-adult colony at `base_spawn_rate=0.35`, then resetting to a clean 2-adult colony: with the reused carry the new colony produced 1 berried female on day 1, while a clean 2-adult colony produced 0. Clear the accumulator whenever spawning continuity is broken.
amendments.rationale: This is a correctness bug in the new deterministic reproduction bookkeeping: rounding memory is leaking across colony resets and changes the outcome for later populations.

amendments.body: Reset `hatch_success_carry` whenever all berried females / egg cohorts are cleared. The accumulator is also persisted in `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:128-131`, but `egg_development()` reuses it at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:517-520` and can return with no cohorts at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:465-475` without zeroing it; `clamp_berried_to_adults()` at `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:546-553` can also delete cohorts without touching the carry. That lets a brand-new clutch inherit old fractional hatch credit. I reproduced this with `hatch_success_base=0.3`: after one large cohort left a positive carry, a later single-cohort state hatched 2 juveniles immediately, while the same clean single-cohort state hatched 0. Clear the carry whenever the hatch process loses continuity.
amendments.rationale: This is the same class of state-leak bug as the spawn carry, but on the hatch path. It produces impossible early hatches that are not attributable to the current clutch.

payload.summary: Reviewed the committed implementation and key files end-to-end across gas exchange, engine/state/save, snapshot/API, scenarios, and shrimp reproduction. `cargo test -q` passed, but I found 2 correctness bugs in the new deterministic shrimp reproduction bookkeeping: the persisted spawn and hatch carry accumulators survive colony/cohort resets and can make later unrelated populations reproduce or hatch earlier than a clean state.
